chapter: Telephone reels: blues and Bessie Smith
title: Jealousy among musicians
summary: He says jealousy exists among all musicians but he never felt threatened.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: You bet. Did you ever find -- you know, I've always wondered about this because to me you're in a class by yourself. Did you ever find any jealousy from co-musicians or friends or workers when you were really hot?

Well, I tell you, the -- that jealousy exists in all classes of musicians. All classes of musicians have that little quirk that they -- that they have. And it's more prevalent in some than it is in others. That's all. It comes out clearer. And so you have to wait a minute so you can find out which way it's coming out. That's all it is.
Uh-huh. See, I only knew you, you know, when you -- when you were older. I didn't know you when you were younger. I sure wish I knew you years ago, though, but

you strike me -- this could be, you know, this could be maybe you in your latter years or maybe I -- see, just as I say -- I always say you're in a class by yourself. I think -- and I know you're saying to be jealous is human and still -- but I just wondered how -- did you feel that way about yourself with others? Did you feel threatened or whatever?
See, I didn't really think so, J. C.
No, I never felt threatened at all.
I never -- I really felt that. And it's like you're such a human -- you're such a person person, you know, and you know that there's room for everybody.
Excuse me. I have to -- excuse this coughing every once in a while.
That's okay. Do you want to get a drink of water?
You okay? Yeah, it's -- it's prevalent in -- I think the more insecure the artist, you know, the more prevalent it is. I don't know. What do you think?
Well, I've never felt that way, so I don't know.
